Classical Hurwitz–Radon construction and Adams sphere vector-field bound
correctness.rationale: Nonemptiness in dimension three follows from the displayed exact collision and constant determinant; adjoining identity coordinates preserves both. On every admissible linear family derivative evaluation at zero is injective and sends its punctured space to nonsingular matrices, so the real matrix bound applies even if finite dimension was not assumed. Independently, the bound follows from Adams's sphere vector-field theorem: normalize the matrix space to contain I, then for each unit x project the remaining basis images A_i x onto x-perp. Any dependence would give a nonzero matrix in the space killing x. Conversely the Hurwitz–Radon skew, pairwise anticommuting generators give A^T A=(sum of squared coefficients)I, and hence an invertible-output space containing I. For any fixed eligible F, composing on the output preserves its real collisions and multiplies its constant Jacobian determinant by det A. The map from the matrix space is linear and injective and contains F via I. This proves both sharpness and pointwise attainment; odd n gives rho(n)=1, and even n>=4 gives rho(n)>=2, with no assertion for n=2.
residual_risks: The independent calculation checks the seed, not the classical all-dimensional matrix theorems, which are used analytically.

originality.rationale: The known exact invariant is for real matrix spaces. The prior polynomial lineability paper gives the odd-real obstruction and leaves even-real 2-lineability open. The frozen result identifies the matrix invariant with the noninjective polynomial one via both evaluation and a collision-preserving lift through an arbitrary seed. The defensible novelty is that identification and its application to the stated question, not the Hurwitz–Radon function, its sample values, or the odd-real maximum.
residual_risks: The precise polynomial lift could have appeared independently elsewhere; the indexed evidence does not establish historical priority. Original bodies of the matrix papers were not recovered, so absence of a polynomial application from their complete texts is not asserted.
